app.title: LitePhospho — Explainable Phosphosite Predictor
app.summary: A person pastes a protein sequence or loads an example, sets a decision threshold, and runs the trained model to score every candidate acceptor residue. Counts of length, candidate sites and predicted sites appear, along with the sequence with predicted sites shaded by probability and a table listing every site's position, residue, probability and call. The person then picks one site and sees its surrounding window of residues coloured by how much masking each one lowers the prediction. What they get is a set of per-site calls and, for each site they choose, an explanation of which neighbouring residues drove the call.

task.text: Predict which serine, threonine and tyrosine residues in a protein are phosphorylated, and show which neighbouring residues drove each prediction.

data.text: A protein sequence, with model-scored candidate sites and an importance profile for each site over a fixed window around it.
data.item: a candidate S/T/Y residue in a protein sequence, with its 31-residue context window

stage.text: screening a protein sequence for likely modification sites, before experimental follow-up

mechanism.text: A threshold slider in the sidebar drives both the shaded sequence and the per-site table, and summary counts update to match. A site chosen from a dropdown opens its context window, coloured by occlusion importance, with the site itself outlined.

field.text: explainable deep-learning prediction of post-translational modification sites in bioinformatics

workflow.name: score every candidate position in a sequence with a model and explain one call

steps.here: Paste a one-letter amino-acid sequence into the text box, or press 'Load example' to fill it with a seeded protein fragment.

steps.step: set the cut-off that turns a score into a call
steps.here: The sidebar 'Decision threshold' slider (0–1, step 0.05) sets which probabilities count as a predicted phosphosite, and changing it re-colours the results without rerunning the model.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Predict phosphosites' finds every S/T/Y, takes a ±15 X-padded window around each one, and runs the ONNX model to get one probability per site.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Metrics show sequence length, candidate sites and sites above the threshold. The sequence is redrawn with predicted sites in bold and shaded green by probability, and hovering a site shows its position and score.

steps.step: read each item's values in a list
steps.here: A table lists each site's position, residue, rounded probability and its 'Phosphosite' or '—' call.

Choosing a site from the dropdown computes an occlusion profile: each residue in the 31-residue window is masked in turn, and the window is drawn with residues shaded by the drop in probability and the centre site outlined in purple.

distinctive: Only the acceptor residues S, T and Y are candidates. Each one is scored from a fixed 31-residue window padded with X at the sequence ends.

Explanations come from occlusion (deletion) rather than gradients. Each window position is masked and the drop in probability is taken as its importance, computed lazily and cached for the selected site only.
The threshold is applied after scoring, so moving the slider changes the calls and counts without running the model again.
